newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Mayor says limiting abatement would hurt.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Mayor says limiting abatement would hurt.

text.p: Cleveland Mayor Michael White said Thursday approval of a ballot initiative next month limiting tax abatements would compromise the city's ability to compete for businesses.
The special election for the amendment is Aug 5.

Cleveland Teachers Union has sponsored the initiative, which would require either the city or a company requesting a new property tax abatement to reimburse the financially troubled public schools for tax revenues lost.
The initiative would hurt Cleveland's ability to compete with wealthier suburban neighbors and limit the city's use of abatements to aid development of distressed areas and brownfields, White said.
"If income taxes decline, city services will suffer and ultimately a tax increase will be needed to continue to provide decent services and recapture lost revenues," White said.
Cleveland lost four businesses and 462 jobs in 1996 to suburbs offering abatements, according to the mayor's office.
Ohio lawmakers have approved legislation allowing White to take control of the Cleveland public schools. The bill awaits Gov. George Voinovich's signature.
